monitoring.tpl.cpu_usage_cores.descripti: Real-time CPU cores consumed by the dev instance container.
monitoring.tpl.cpu_usage_cores.title: CPU Usage
monitoring.tpl.disk_read_bytes.descripti: Container disk read rate. Sustained high = data is not cached in memory and is read from disk repeatedly.
monitoring.tpl.disk_read_bytes.title: Disk Read Rate
monitoring.tpl.disk_write_bytes.descript: Container disk write rate. Spikes when saving checkpoints / writing data to disk.
monitoring.tpl.disk_write_bytes.title: Disk Write Rate
monitoring.tpl.dyn_cancellation_rate.des: Worker request cancellation rate (dynamo_component_cancellation_total). Cancellations from client disconnects/timeouts; sustained > 0 = the upstream timeout is too tight or the backend is too slow. (Note: dynamo has no success/failure label, so the cancellation rate is used instead of a success rate.)
monitoring.tpl.dyn_detokenize_us_per_tok: Average frontend detokenization time per token in microseconds (detokenize_total_us / detokenize_token_count). Post-processing overhead of streaming output.
Number of client connections the frontend has seen disconnect (dynamo_frontend_disconnected_clients). A sudden increase = many upstream disconnects/timeouts.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_enqueue_rejected.desc: Rate of requests rejected because the queue is full (dynamo_work_handler_enqueue_rejected_total). > 0 = overloaded and dropping requests; you must add replicas/scale out.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_first_response_p95.de: P95 from the work handler receiving a request to its first response (dynamo_work_handler_time_to_first_response_seconds). Backend processing start-up latency.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_frontend_qps.descript: Request rate at the frontend entry (dynamo_component_router_requests_total). The real external QPS.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_frontend_qps.title: Frontend QPS (req/s)
monitoring.tpl.dyn_gpu_cache_usage.descr: GPU KV cache occupancy ratio (dynamo_component_gpu_cache_usage_percent). Close to 100 means it is about to overflow/preempt.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_gpu_cache_usage.title: GPU KV Cache Usage
monitoring.tpl.dyn_inflight.description: Number of requests the worker is currently processing (inflight). Measures concurrent load.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_inflight.title: In-flight Requests
monitoring.tpl.dyn_input_seq_p95.descrip: Request prompt token count P95 (dynamo_component_router_input_sequence_tokens). Shows the input load distribution.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_input_seq_p95.title: Input Sequence Length P95 (tokens)
monitoring.tpl.dyn_itl_p95.description: Inter-token latency P95 (inter_token_latency). Streaming smoothness; high = decode stalls.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_itl_p95.title: ITL P95 (s)
monitoring.tpl.dyn_kv_hit_rate.descripti: Average router KV cache hit rate (dynamo_component_router_kv_hit_rate). Higher reuse saves more compute.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_kv_hit_rate.title: KV Cache Hit Rate
monitoring.tpl.dyn_kv_transfer_p95.descr: Router-estimated KV block transfer latency P95 (dynamo_component_router_kv_transfer_estimated_latency_seconds). Only meaningful for disaggregated deployments (separate prefill/decode).
monitoring.tpl.dyn_kv_transfer_p95.title: KV Transfer Latency P95 (s)
monitoring.tpl.dyn_model_context_len.des: Maximum context length of the model (dynamo_frontend_model_context_length). Static config, for confirming the deployment parameters.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_model_load_time.descr: Time the worker spends loading model weights (dynamo_component_model_load_time_seconds). For observing cold starts; a sudden increase = larger weights/slower storage.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_model_load_time.title: Model Load Time (s)
monitoring.tpl.dyn_model_total_kv_blocks: Total number of KV cache blocks available to the model (dynamo_frontend_model_total_kv_blocks). Static config, the GPU memory budget cap.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_output_seq_p95.descri: Generated token count P95 (dynamo_component_router_output_sequence_tokens). Shows the output length distribution, which affects GPU memory/duration.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_output_seq_p95.title: Output Sequence Length P95 (tokens)
monitoring.tpl.dyn_permit_wait_p95.descr: P95 of the time requests wait for a concurrency permit (dynamo_work_handler_permit_wait_seconds). High = queueing due to concurrency limits; the pool capacity is not enough.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_permit_wait_p95.title: Permit Wait P95 (s)
monitoring.tpl.dyn_pool_active.descripti: Number of currently active tasks in the work handler pool (dynamo_work_handler_pool_active_tasks). Close to the pool capacity = concurrency is saturated.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_pool_active.title: Worker Pool Active Tasks
monitoring.tpl.dyn_pool_capacity.descrip: Work handler pool capacity limit (dynamo_work_handler_pool_capacity). Read with the active tasks to see saturation.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_pool_capacity.title: Worker Pool Capacity
monitoring.tpl.dyn_queue_capacity.descri: Work handler queue capacity limit (dynamo_work_handler_queue_capacity). Read with the queue depth to see the backlog ratio.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_queue_capacity.title: Queue Capacity
monitoring.tpl.dyn_queue_depth.descripti: Number of requests backlogged in the work handler queue. Sustained > 0 = concurrency has hit its limit; consider adding replicas/nodes.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_queue_depth.title: Queue Depth
monitoring.tpl.dyn_request_rate.descript: Requests processed per second by the worker backend (rate of dynamo_component_requests_total). The primary throughput metric.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_request_rate.title: Request Rate (req/s)
monitoring.tpl.dyn_router_overhead_p95.d: P95 of the total router routing time (dynamo_router_overhead_total_ms). Includes hashing/lookup/scheduling; if it is a large share of TTFT, the router needs optimizing.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_router_sched_p95.desc: P95 of the scheduling time the router spends choosing a worker (dynamo_router_overhead_scheduling_ms). High = router decisions are becoming the bottleneck.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_shared_cache_hit.desc: Average router cross-request shared prefix cache hit rate (dynamo_component_router_shared_cache_hit_rate). High = good reuse, saving prefill.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_tokenize_p95.descript: Frontend prompt tokenize time P95 (dynamo_frontend_tokenize_seconds). CPU preprocessing; high = long prompts / a CPU bottleneck.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_tokenize_p95.title: Tokenize Time P95 (s)
monitoring.tpl.dyn_total_blocks.descript: Total KV cache block capacity of the worker (dynamo_component_total_blocks). Read with the GPU cache usage to see the remaining space.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_total_blocks.title: Total KV Blocks
monitoring.tpl.dyn_ttft_p95.description: Time to first token P95 (frontend dynamo_component_router_time_to_first_token_seconds). The wait users perceive.
monitoring.tpl.dyn_ttft_p95.title: TTFT P95 (s)
monitoring.tpl.dyn_uptime.title: Uptime (s)
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_board_limit_viol: Time a single GPU was throttled by board-level limits (TDP/current cap).
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_dec_util.descrip: NVDEC video decoder usage of a single GPU. High during video dataset preprocessing (decoding mp4).
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_dec_util.title: Decoder Utilization
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_dram_active.desc: Memory controller activity of a single GPU (similar to mem_util). High = memory bandwidth is tight.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_ecc_dbe_agg.desc: Aggregate DBE of a single GPU. Anything > 0 = the GPU must be replaced.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_ecc_dbe_vol.desc: Cumulative ECC double-bit errors of a single GPU (fatal). Anything > 0 = GPUMemoryErrorDetected alert; the GPU memory is physically damaged.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_ecc_sbe_agg.desc: Aggregate SBE of a single GPU (permanent count across restarts). Long-term accumulation shows GPU memory aging.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_ecc_sbe_vol.desc: Cumulative ECC single-bit errors of a single GPU. Single-bit errors are correctable and occasional ones are normal; a burst in a short time = the GPU memory is about to fail.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_enc_util.descrip: NVENC video encoder usage of a single GPU. 0 for AI training; only used by video transcoding jobs.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_enc_util.title: Encoder Utilization
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_fb_free.descript: Free memory of a single GPU. fb_total - fb_used. Also check this when memory fragmentation makes large chunk allocations fail.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_fb_free.title: Free GPU Memory
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_fp16_active.desc: FP16 pipe activity of a single GPU. Highly correlated with tensor_active.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_fp32_active.desc: FP32 pipe activity of a single GPU. Used by older training code or kernels without mixed precision.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_fp64_active.desc: FP64 pipe activity of a single GPU. Almost 0 for AI training (which uses FP16/BF16); commonly used only by HPC.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_gr_engine_active: Graphics/compute engine active ratio of a single GPU. Another view of overall compute usage (more accurate than GPU_UTIL, excludes waiting).
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_low_util_violati: A single GPU automatically lowering clocks due to low utilization (power saving). Should not happen under training load.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_mem_clock.descri: Memory clock of a single GPU in MHz.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_mem_clock.title: Memory Clock
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_mem_used_gib.des: Memory used on a single GPU, in GiB. L4 = 24 / A10 = 24 / H100 = 80. Close to the limit = on the edge of OOM.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_mem_util.descrip: How busy the memory controller of a single GPU is. High = memory bandwidth is saturated; low + low GPU_util = the GPU is idle.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_mem_util.title: GPU Memory Controller Busy
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_memory_temp.desc: HBM memory temperature of a single GPU. Moves with the core temperature; > 95 is dangerous.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_nvlink_bandwidth: NVLink L0 active data bandwidth of a single GPU (header + payload). The main bandwidth source for multi-GPU AllReduce; only on multi-GPU interconnect GPUs such as B300.
Cumulative bandwidth over all NVLink lanes of a single GPU (only on multi-GPU interconnect GPUs, e.g. B300).
NVLink data CRC errors of a single GPU (data integrity issue).
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_nvlink_errors.de: Cumulative NVLink replay + recovery errors of a single GPU. Thresholds: replay > 10 / recovery > 0 = NVLinkErrorsDetected alert. An unstable interconnect directly slows down DDP training.
NVLink flit CRC errors of a single GPU (physical-layer error rate).
NVLink recovery count of a single GPU (> 0 = the link has been disconnected).
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_nvlink_replay.de: NVLink replay count of a single GPU.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_pcie_replay.desc: PCIe replay count of a single GPU. Occasional 0-10 is normal; a steadily growing count = an unstable PCIe physical layer (loose connection / motherboard fault).
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_pcie_rx_bytes.de: Host→GPU PCIe inbound bandwidth of a single GPU. The main traffic during data loading.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_pcie_tx_bytes.de: GPU→host PCIe outbound bandwidth of a single GPU. Short spikes during checkpoints / loss reduce.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_power.descriptio: Current instantaneous power draw of a single GPU in W. L4 = 72 / A10 = 150 / H100 = 700. 80-90% of the rated value at training steady state is normal.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_power.title: GPU Power
Cumulative microseconds a single GPU was throttled for exceeding the power limit. > 100 = GPUPowerViolation alert (PSU/cooling problem).
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_reliability_viol: Reliability throttling of a single GPU (hardware health issue). Non-zero = contact the hardware team.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_remap_correctabl: Correctable row remaps of a single GPU (HBM row-level repair, A100+ only).
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_remap_failure.de: Remap failures of a single GPU. > 0 = the GPU should be retired; take it offline and replace it immediately.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_remap_uncorrecta: Uncorrectable row remaps of a single GPU. > 0 = GPU memory is deteriorating.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_retired_dbe.desc: Pages retired due to DBE on a single GPU. Anything > 0 = severe.
Pages pending retirement on a single GPU (takes effect only after a restart).
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_retired_sbe.desc: Pages retired due to SBE on a single GPU (isolated bad pages). Many = GPU memory aging is accelerating.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_sm_active.descri: Warp active ratio of the SMs (streaming multiprocessors) of a single GPU. Read it together with occupancy: active = warps are running, occupancy = warp count relative to the maximum.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_sm_active.title: SM Activity
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_sm_clock.descrip: Real-time SM clock of a single GPU in MHz. Should be close to the boost clock during stable training.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_sm_clock.title: SM Clock
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_sm_occupancy.des: SM warp occupancy of a single GPU (active warps / SM maximum). Measures kernel parallelism. High = kernels fill the SMs; low = poor kernel design or cooperative launch not enabled.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_sync_boost_viola: Clock sync violation of a single GPU. Clocks are inconsistent across GPUs, usually due to an NVLink/PCIe fault.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_temp.description: GPU core temperature of a single GPU in °C. Thresholds: > 80 warning (GPUHighTemperature), > 85 critical (GPUCriticalTemperature). High = poor data center cooling or an aging GPU.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_temp.title: GPU Temperature
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_tensor_active.de: Tensor Core (HMMA) active ratio of a single GPU. Should be high for mixed-precision training; low = Tensor Cores are not being used and compute is wasted.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_thermal_violatio: Cumulative microseconds a single GPU was throttled for exceeding the temperature limit. Any data within 5min = a cooling problem.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_total_energy.des: Cumulative energy of a single GPU in mJ. Power integrated over time. Used for cost estimation.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_util.description: Compute busy rate of a single GPU. Ideal for training is 80-95%; < 50% = the GPU is idle and data/communication is slow; staying flat at 100% for too long is not necessarily efficient either; SM_active is what really counts.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_util.title: GPU Utilization
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_xid_errors.descr: Cumulative NVIDIA XID error codes of a single GPU. > 0 = GPUXidError alert. Different codes mean different things (XID 13 = GR engine / 31 = ECC); check dmesg for details.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_card_xid_errors.title: XID Errors Total
monitoring.tpl.gpu_mem_copy_util.descrip: How busy the memory controller is. High = memory bandwidth is saturated; low + low GPU_util = the GPU is idle.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_mem_copy_util.title: GPU Memory Controller Busy
monitoring.tpl.gpu_mem_used_gib.descript: Memory used per GPU. Close to the GPU limit when loading a large model/large batch = OOM risk.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_mem_used_gib.title: GPU Memory Used
monitoring.tpl.gpu_temp.description: Per-GPU temperature. Staying >85°C triggers throttling and reduces compute.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_temp.title: GPU Temperature
monitoring.tpl.gpu_util.description: Utilization of the GPUs used by this dev instance. Rises while debugging/training and is close to 0 when idle.
monitoring.tpl.gpu_util.title: GPU Utilization
monitoring.tpl.inf_cpu_usage_cores.descr: CPU usage of the inference Pod; high = heavy tokenize / detokenize.
monitoring.tpl.inf_cpu_usage_cores.title: CPU Usage (cores)
monitoring.tpl.inf_gpu_mem_used_gib.desc: Per-GPU memory. Mostly consumed by the model weights + KV cache.
monitoring.tpl.inf_gpu_power.title: GPU Power (W)
monitoring.tpl.inf_gpu_temp.title: GPU Temperature (°C)
monitoring.tpl.inf_gpu_util.description: Per-GPU compute utilization. Low when inference is idle, high under load testing.
monitoring.tpl.inf_gpu_util.title: GPU Utilization (%)
monitoring.tpl.inf_mem_usage_gib.descrip: Memory of the inference Pod. The KV cache lives in GPU memory; this is the host-side buffer + tokenizer.
monitoring.tpl.inf_mem_usage_gib.title: Memory Usage (GiB)
monitoring.tpl.inf_model_concurrent.desc: Number of requests the gateway is currently processing concurrently. Reflects instantaneous load pressure.
monitoring.tpl.inf_model_latency_p90.des: End-to-end latency p90 measured at the gateway entry (only successful 2xx requests, including the network). The latency baseline for the external SLA.
monitoring.tpl.inf_model_qps.description: POST invocation rate at the gateway entry. The real external QPS (including the network layer), closer to what users experience than the internal sglang engine counters.
monitoring.tpl.inf_model_qps.title: Invocation Rate (QPS)
monitoring.tpl.inf_model_replicas_active: Number of replica Pods that actually received traffic in the last 5m (rate > 0). Fewer than total replicas = some replicas are idle, a sign that KEDA will scale in.
Number of replica Pods seen in the last 5m (counted by model_invocations). Reflects the current deployment size of the endpoint.
monitoring.tpl.inf_model_success_rate.de: Success rate% = (1 - error rate). The most important SLO of an inference service. Uses or vector(0) to avoid division by zero. Investigate if it stays < 99.
monitoring.tpl.inf_model_ttfb_p90.descri: Time To First Byte p90 measured at the gateway, 2xx only. The primary metric for perceived streaming responsiveness.
monitoring.tpl.inf_model_ttfb_p90.title: TTFB P90
monitoring.tpl.inf_net_rx_bytes.descript: Request byte stream received by the inference Pod.
monitoring.tpl.inf_net_rx_bytes.title: Network Ingress (B/s)
monitoring.tpl.inf_net_tx_bytes.descript: Response byte stream returned by the inference Pod.
monitoring.tpl.inf_net_tx_bytes.title: Network Egress (B/s)
monitoring.tpl.inf_nginx_errors.descript: Errors from the reverse-proxy nginx-lua-prometheus itself (not application request errors). Sustained > 0 = the gateway component is abnormal.
monitoring.tpl.inf_nginx_errors.title: nginx Internal Errors
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_cache_hit_rate.de: RadixAttention KV reuse rate in GPU memory. Should be high (0.5+) for RAG / shared system prompts.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_e2e_p50.title: E2E Latency P50 (s)
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_e2e_p95.descripti: End-to-end total request duration P95. Covers the whole queue + prefill + decode path. This is the metric SLOs are measured against.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_e2e_p95.title: E2E Latency P95 (s)
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_e2e_p99.descripti: End-to-end P99; check this for the SLO long tail.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_e2e_p99.title: E2E Latency P99 (s)
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_gen_throughput.de: Tokens generated per second in the SGLang decode phase. The primary performance metric.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_generation_tokens: Cumulative average tokens generated per request (sum/count). Related to the max_tokens setting.
Rate of cumulative generated tokens, complementary to gen_throughput (which only has values while active).
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_http_active.descr: Number of currently active HTTP connections on the SGLang engine (engine view, different from gateway concurrency).
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_http_active.title: Active HTTP Connections
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_http_requests_rat: HTTP request rate broken down by endpoint, with health-check/self-monitoring paths filtered out.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_http_responses_ra: Response rate broken down by status_code (health-check paths filtered out); use it to watch the 5xx/4xx error rate.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_kv_available_toke: Number of completely free slots in the KV pool. Close to 0 = preemption is imminent.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_kv_capacity.descr: Total capacity of the SGLang KV cache pool (max_total_num_tokens). Read with kv_used to get the occupancy; a larger cap allows more concurrency.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_kv_capacity.title: KV Pool Capacity
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_kv_evictable_toke: Number of prefix cache slots that can be evicted by LRU (radix-cached). Larger = more reusable space.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_kv_used_tokens.de: Number of allocated KV cache token slots (occupied by running requests).
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_prefill_forward_p: P95 of the pure prefill forward phase (excluding queue), measures compute density.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_prompt_tokens_avg: Cumulative average input tokens (sum/count). Uses cumulative values so the historical average is still shown instead of a blank when there is no traffic.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_queue_p50.title: Queue Time P50 (s)
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_queue_p95.descrip: Request queue wait P95. A value of several seconds means pressure is high; add replicas or raise max_running_requests.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_queue_p95.title: Queue Time P95 (s)
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_queue_reqs.descri: Number of requests waiting to be scheduled. Sustained > 0 means concurrency has hit its limit; consider adding replicas or lowering the batch size.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_queue_reqs.title: Queued Requests
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_request_process_p: P95 of the request intake (request_process) phase, time spent on tokenize + dispatch.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_running_reqs.desc: Number of requests SGLang is currently processing. Measures concurrent load.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_token_usage.descr: KV cache token occupancy ratio; close to 1 means it is about to overflow / preempt.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_token_usage.title: KV Cache Usage
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_ttft_p50.descript: Median time to first token. Half of the requests are faster than this value.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_ttft_p50.title: TTFT P50 (s)
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_ttft_p95.descript: Time to first token P95. Time spent in the prefill phase, including prompt parsing + the first batch forward. The few seconds users wait before text appears are mostly spent here.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_ttft_p95.title: TTFT P95 (s)
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_ttft_p99.descript: Time to first token P99, the long tail of slow requests.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_ttft_p99.title: TTFT P99 (s)
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_uncached_prompt_t: Cumulative average prompt tokens that missed the prefix cache (sum/count). Lower = the cache is more effective.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_utilization.descr: Overall utilization of the SGLang engine. Combines how busy batch occupancy / KV / scheduling are, showing whether the engine is saturated.
monitoring.tpl.inf_sgl_utilization.title: Engine Utilization
monitoring.tpl.job_active_pods.descripti: Number of Pods currently alive for the K8s Job (excluding init / Pending).
monitoring.tpl.job_active_pods.title: Active Pods
monitoring.tpl.job_board_limit_violation: Increase in throttling time of the job's GPUs triggered by board limits.
monitoring.tpl.job_cpu_throttled_seconds: Rate of CFS-throttled time across all Pods of the job. Sustained > 0 = the CPU limit is the bottleneck; the dataloader / data preprocessing is slowed down, indirectly starving the GPUs.
monitoring.tpl.job_cpu_usage_cores.descr: Sum of CPU usage across all Pods (in cores). High = heavy data preprocessing (tokenize, augmentation). Staying close to the limits for long slows down feeding data to the GPUs.
monitoring.tpl.job_cpu_usage_cores.title: CPU Usage
monitoring.tpl.job_disk_read_bytes.descr: Sum of disk read rate across all Pods. High while the dataset is loaded from local disk; sustained high = data is not cached in memory and the dataloader re-reads it every epoch.
monitoring.tpl.job_disk_read_bytes.title: Disk Read Rate
monitoring.tpl.job_disk_write_bytes.desc: Sum of disk write rate across all Pods. Spikes for a few seconds during checkpoints; sustained high = logs are written too often or there are many tmp files.
monitoring.tpl.job_ecc_dbe_total.descrip: Cumulative uncorrectable ECC errors (double-bit) of the job's GPUs. > 0 = a GPU memory hardware fault; the GPU should be replaced.
monitoring.tpl.job_ecc_dbe_total.title: ECC Double-Bit Errors
monitoring.tpl.job_ecc_sbe_total.descrip: Increase in correctable ECC errors of the job's GPUs. Occasional errors are normal; a surge = the GPU memory is starting to age.
monitoring.tpl.job_ecc_sbe_total.title: ECC Single-Bit Errors
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_impaired_remote.d: Increase in impaired remote connection events. > 0 = EFA on the peer node is abnormal.
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_info.description: Number of EFA device info entries (marks presence).
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_info.title: EFA Device Count
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_lifespan.title: EFA Uptime
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_rdma_read_resp_by: EFA RDMA read response byte rate.
Increase in EFA RDMA read work request errors.
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_rdma_read_wrs.des: EFA RDMA read work request rate.
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_rdma_total.descri: EFA RDMA read + write total bandwidth. The main bandwidth source for multi-node LLM training (AllReduce over RDMA).
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_rdma_total.title: EFA RDMA Total Bandwidth
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_rdma_write_recv_b: EFA RDMA write-with-imm receive byte rate.
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_rdma_write_wr_err: Increase in EFA RDMA write work request errors.
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_rdma_write_wrs.de: EFA RDMA write work request rate.
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_recv_bytes.title: EFA Recv Bytes
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_recv_wrs.title: EFA Recv WR
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_retrans_pkts.desc: Increase in EFA retransmitted packets. Sustained > 0 = poor interconnect quality, slowing down all-reduce.
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_retrans_timeout.d: Increase in EFA retransmit timeout events. > 0 = a serious interconnect problem.
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_rx_bytes.descript: EFA receive byte rate (aggregated over node interfaces).
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_rx_bytes.title: EFA Receive Bandwidth
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_rx_drops.descript: Increase in EFA receive packet drops. > 0 = an interconnect problem.
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_rx_drops.title: EFA Packet Drops
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_rx_pkts.title: EFA Receive Packet Rate
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_send_bytes.title: EFA Send Bytes
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_send_wrs.title: EFA Send WR
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_tx_bytes.title: EFA Transmit Bandwidth
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_tx_pkts.title: EFA Transmit Packet Rate
monitoring.tpl.job_efa_unresponsive_remo: Increase in unresponsive remote events. > 0 = the peer node is unreachable.
monitoring.tpl.job_energy_total.descript: Energy rate across all GPUs (mJ/s). Accumulated × time = total electricity (kWh), used to estimate training cost (kWh × electricity price).
monitoring.tpl.job_energy_total.title: Total Energy
monitoring.tpl.job_failed_pods.descripti: Cumulative number of failed Pods of the Job.
monitoring.tpl.job_failed_pods.title: Failed Pods
monitoring.tpl.job_gpu_dram_active_avg.d: Average activity of the GPU memory read/write controller. Sustained > 80% = a memory bandwidth bottleneck where compute waits for data; too low + low compute = idle.
Sum of GPU memory used across all GPUs (in GiB). Shows the combined footprint of model + batch + activations. Close to total capacity (e.g. 4×L4 = 96GB) means you are on the edge of OOM; reduce the batch size, enable ZeRO or use activation checkpointing.
monitoring.tpl.job_gpu_mem_util_avg.desc: How busy the GPU memory controller is (how often HBM memory is read/written). Related to whether memory bandwidth is saturated. Often 70-90% when training large models; staying < 30% usually means the job is compute-bound (the SMs cannot keep up), not memory-bound.
monitoring.tpl.job_gpu_temp_max.descript: Temperature of the hottest GPU in the job. Watch the cooling when it approaches the throttling threshold (usually 80-85°C).
monitoring.tpl.job_gpu_temp_max.title: GPU Max Temperature
monitoring.tpl.job_gpu_util_avg.descript: Average busy rate across all GPUs. Should hold steady at 80-95% during training. Staying below 50% means data loading or inter-GPU communication is stalling; check the dataloader config (num_workers / pin_memory) and the network topology.
monitoring.tpl.job_gpu_util_avg.title: GPU Avg Utilization
monitoring.tpl.job_gr_engine_avg.descrip: Average graphics/compute engine active ratio across all GPUs of the job. More accurate than GPU_UTIL (excludes waiting).
monitoring.tpl.job_gr_engine_avg.title: Graphics Engine Avg Activity
monitoring.tpl.job_mem_usage_gib.descrip: Sum of memory usage across all Pods. Close to the limits = OOM risk. Dataset cache, model weights and activations all consume this.
monitoring.tpl.job_mem_usage_gib.title: Memory Usage
monitoring.tpl.job_net_rx_dropped.descri: Inbound packet drop rate across all Pods of the job. > 0 = network congestion or insufficient buffers; AllReduce in distributed training may retransmit repeatedly and slow down.
monitoring.tpl.job_net_rx_dropped.title: Network Ingress Drops
monitoring.tpl.job_net_tx_dropped.descri: Outbound packet drop rate across all Pods of the job. > 0 = congestion on the sending side; checkpoint uploads / gradient sync may be impeded.
monitoring.tpl.job_net_tx_dropped.title: Network Egress Drops
monitoring.tpl.job_network_rx_bytes.desc: Sum of inbound traffic across all Pods. Sources: data pulled from S3 + AllReduce results from other ranks. DDP training shows sustained high traffic with periodic spikes.
monitoring.tpl.job_network_tx_bytes.desc: Sum of outbound traffic across all Pods. Checkpoint uploads + AllReduce sends + monitoring reports.
monitoring.tpl.job_oom_events.descriptio: Cumulative OOMKilled rate across all Pods of the job. > 0 = a container was OOM-killed by the kernel, most likely due to an oversized batch/sequence or a host memory leak outside GPU memory. A healthy training job should stay at 0.
monitoring.tpl.job_oom_events.title: OOM Count
monitoring.tpl.job_pod_count.description: Number of Pods currently alive for the job. For a single-node, single-Pod job it should be 1; for multi-node DDP it equals the node count. Fewer than expected = some Pods are still being scheduled.
monitoring.tpl.job_pod_count.title: Pod Count
monitoring.tpl.job_power_violation.descr: Increase in throttling time of the job's GPUs triggered by the power cap. > 0 = hitting the power wall and lowering clocks.
monitoring.tpl.job_power_violation.title: Power Throttling
monitoring.tpl.job_remap_failure.descrip: Row remap failure flag of the job's GPUs. > 0 = the GPU memory repair mechanism has failed; replace the GPU urgently.
monitoring.tpl.job_remap_failure.title: Remap Failure
monitoring.tpl.job_remap_uncorrectable.d: Increase in uncorrectable row remaps of the job's GPUs. > 0 = GPU memory is deteriorating.
monitoring.tpl.job_sm_active_avg.descrip: Average active ratio of the streaming multiprocessors (SMs) on the GPUs. High = compute is saturated; low while GPU_util is high = single-threaded kernels are not exploiting enough parallelism.
monitoring.tpl.job_sm_active_avg.title: SM Avg Activity
monitoring.tpl.job_sm_clock_avg.descript: Average SM clock across all GPUs of the job. Below the rated clock = throttling (check the temperature/power violations).
monitoring.tpl.job_sm_clock_avg.title: SM Avg Clock
monitoring.tpl.job_sm_occupancy_avg.desc: Average SM warp occupancy across all GPUs of the job. Shows whether parallelism is saturated.
monitoring.tpl.job_succeeded_pods.descri: Cumulative number of Pods of the Job that completed successfully.
monitoring.tpl.job_succeeded_pods.title: Succeeded Pods
monitoring.tpl.job_tensor_active_avg.des: Average Tensor Core usage (% of time running matrix multiplications). This is the core compute metric for LLM/Transformer workloads (an approximation of MFU). Efficient training should be > 30-50%; too low means mixed precision (FP16/BF16) is not used or the kernels are poorly designed.
monitoring.tpl.job_thermal_violation.des: Increase in throttling time of the job's GPUs triggered by temperature. > 0 = insufficient cooling is slowing down compute.
monitoring.tpl.job_total_oom.description: Rate at which the job is OOMKilled. > 0 = the memory limits are not enough; reduce the batch size or raise the limits.
monitoring.tpl.job_total_oom.title: Total OOM
monitoring.tpl.job_total_power.descripti: Sum of the current instantaneous power draw across all GPUs (W). E.g. 4 L4 GPUs at full load draw about 280W. For sudden spikes or lower-than-expected values, check the power-saving/throttling violation metrics.
monitoring.tpl.job_total_power.title: Total Power
monitoring.tpl.job_total_restarts.descri: Cumulative restart count across all Pods of the job. > 0 = NCCL/OOM/Xid faults occurred and K8s restarted the Pods.
monitoring.tpl.job_total_restarts.title: Total Pod Restarts
monitoring.tpl.kpi_cpu_core_hours_30d.de: Cumulative CPU core hours consumed by the user over the past 30 days.
monitoring.tpl.kpi_gpu_mem_peak_gib.desc: Peak GPU memory used by this dev instance over the past 24 hours.
monitoring.tpl.kpi_idle_minutes.descript: Minutes in the past 1h during which GPU utilization was below 5%.
monitoring.tpl.kpi_idle_minutes.title: Idle Time (GPU util < 5%)
monitoring.tpl.mem_usage_gib.description: Working set memory of the dev instance container. Approaching the limit gets it OOMKilled.
monitoring.tpl.mem_usage_gib.title: Memory Usage
monitoring.tpl.network_rx_bytes.descript: Container network inbound traffic. Rises when downloading datasets / running pip install.
monitoring.tpl.network_rx_bytes.title: Network Ingress
monitoring.tpl.network_tx_bytes.descript: Container network outbound traffic. Rises when pushing results / uploading models.
monitoring.tpl.network_tx_bytes.title: Network Egress
monitoring.tpl.pod_age_seconds.descripti: Seconds since the Pod started (≈ training run time).
monitoring.tpl.pod_age_seconds.title: Pod Age
monitoring.tpl.pod_container_ready.descr: Number of Ready containers in the Pod. A Pod can have multiple containers (trainer + sidecar); this is the count of Ready containers.
monitoring.tpl.pod_container_ready.title: Containers Ready
monitoring.tpl.pod_container_terminated_: Cumulative number of containers in the Pod that exited abnormally (exit code != 0).
Cumulative number of OOMKilled containers in the Pod. > 0 = adjust the memory limits or reduce the batch size.
monitoring.tpl.pod_container_waiting_cra: Number of containers in CrashLoopBackOff in the Pod. > 0 = containers exit abnormally and K8s keeps restarting them (a bug in the application code).
monitoring.tpl.pod_container_waiting_cre: Number of containers being created in the Pod. Normal for a short time; long = slow init / slow volume mounts.
monitoring.tpl.pod_container_waiting_ima: Number of containers in ImagePullBackOff in the Pod. > 0 = wrong ECR permissions or a wrong image name.
monitoring.tpl.pod_cpu_load_avg_10s.desc: Pod 10-second CPU load (similar to Linux loadavg). Above the container CPU limit = tasks are queueing.
monitoring.tpl.pod_cpu_system_cores.desc: Pod kernel-mode CPU (syscalls: file reads / networking). High = an IO bottleneck, not a CPU compute problem.
monitoring.tpl.pod_cpu_throttled_periods: Throttled periods / total periods = throttle percentage.
monitoring.tpl.pod_cpu_throttled_seconds: Seconds the Pod was throttled by cgroup CFS (for exceeding limits.cpu). > 0 = the limits are too low; add some CPU or reduce num_workers.
monitoring.tpl.pod_cpu_usage_cores.descr: CPU cores used by this Pod. High = data preprocessing workers are running. Close to the limits slows down training.
monitoring.tpl.pod_cpu_usage_cores.title: CPU Usage
monitoring.tpl.pod_cpu_user_cores.descri: Pod user-mode CPU (application code: numpy / pandas / python).
monitoring.tpl.pod_cpu_user_cores.title: User CPU
monitoring.tpl.pod_disk_read_bytes.descr: Pod disk read rate. Related to the dataloader pin_memory + num_workers config. Sustained high = data is not cached in memory.
monitoring.tpl.pod_disk_read_bytes.title: Disk Read Rate
monitoring.tpl.pod_disk_write_bytes.desc: Pod disk write rate. Spikes for a few seconds during checkpoints.
monitoring.tpl.pod_file_descriptors.desc: Number of file descriptors open in the Pod. Steadily growing = files are not being closed; approaching the ulimit causes too-many-open-files.
monitoring.tpl.pod_fs_io_time.descriptio: Pod disk IO wait in seconds. High = the disk is slow and the GPU is waiting for data.
monitoring.tpl.pod_fs_io_time.title: IO Wait
monitoring.tpl.pod_fs_limit_bytes.descri: Pod container fs quota (corresponds to emptyDir.sizeLimit).
monitoring.tpl.pod_fs_limit_bytes.title: Filesystem Limit
monitoring.tpl.pod_fs_reads_iops.descrip: Pod disk read IOPS (operations/second). High when reading many small files (e.g. 100 images per ImageNet batch).
monitoring.tpl.pod_fs_reads_iops.title: Disk Read IOPS
monitoring.tpl.pod_fs_usage_bytes.title: Filesystem Usage
monitoring.tpl.pod_fs_writes_iops.title: Disk Write IOPS
Overall GPU active ratio of the Pod (finer-grained than GPU_UTIL).
monitoring.tpl.pod_gpu_mem_used_gib.desc: GPU memory used by the Pod, in GiB. With DDP the 4 rank Pods should be balanced (difference < 1GB); imbalance = a model sharding bug.
monitoring.tpl.pod_gpu_sm_active.descrip: Average SM warp active ratio of the Pod.
monitoring.tpl.pod_gpu_sm_active.title: SM Activity
monitoring.tpl.pod_gpu_tensor_active.des: Tensor Core usage of the Pod. A key metric for LLM training. Rises significantly with FlashAttention / xFormers.
monitoring.tpl.pod_gpu_util.description: Average busy rate of the GPUs used by this Pod. For multi-rank jobs each Pod should be close to job_gpu_util_avg. One rank far lower = it is a slow node and the global DDP speed is held back by it.
monitoring.tpl.pod_gpu_util.title: GPU Utilization
monitoring.tpl.pod_initialized.descripti: Whether all init containers of the Pod have finished. 0 + Pending = init is stuck (e.g. code-sync is slow to pull code).
monitoring.tpl.pod_initialized.title: Initialized
monitoring.tpl.pod_last_terminated_exitc: Exit code of the most recent container exit in the Pod. 0 = success / 1 = application error / 137 = OOM (128+9) / 139 = segfault.
monitoring.tpl.pod_mem_cache_bytes.descr: Pod page cache. High after a large dataset is warmed up (the kernel caches the files).
monitoring.tpl.pod_mem_cache_bytes.title: Page Cache
monitoring.tpl.pod_mem_failures.descript: Pod memory allocation failure rate (events/s). > 0 = close to OOM.
monitoring.tpl.pod_mem_failures.title: Allocation Failures
monitoring.tpl.pod_mem_max_usage.descrip: Pod historical peak memory (over the current lifecycle). Used for capacity planning.
monitoring.tpl.pod_mem_max_usage.title: Peak Memory Usage
monitoring.tpl.pod_mem_rss_bytes.descrip: Pod RSS in bytes (actual process pages, excludes file cache).
monitoring.tpl.pod_mem_rss_bytes.title: RSS
monitoring.tpl.pod_mem_swap_bytes.descri: Pod swap usage. HyperPod nodes disable swap by default, so it should be 0.
monitoring.tpl.pod_mem_swap_bytes.title: Swap
monitoring.tpl.pod_mem_usage_bytes.descr: Total Pod memory in bytes (includes page cache, larger than working_set).
monitoring.tpl.pod_mem_usage_bytes.title: Total Memory Usage
monitoring.tpl.pod_mem_usage_gib.descrip: Pod working set memory (what the K8s OOMKiller looks at), in GiB. Close to the limits = on the edge of OOM.
monitoring.tpl.pod_mem_usage_gib.title: Working Set Memory
monitoring.tpl.pod_net_rx_dropped.descri: Pod inbound packet drop rate. Sustained > 1 = kernel buffers are insufficient or iptables rejected packets.
monitoring.tpl.pod_net_rx_dropped.title: Ingress Drops
monitoring.tpl.pod_net_rx_errors.descrip: Pod inbound error rate. > 0 = a NIC / link physical-layer problem.
monitoring.tpl.pod_net_rx_errors.title: Ingress Errors
monitoring.tpl.pod_net_rx_packets.descri: Pod inbound packet rate (packets/second). RDMA over EFA does not go through here; see the efa_* metrics.
monitoring.tpl.pod_net_rx_packets.title: Ingress Packets
monitoring.tpl.pod_net_tx_dropped.title: Egress Drops
monitoring.tpl.pod_net_tx_errors.title: Egress Errors
monitoring.tpl.pod_net_tx_packets.title: Egress Packets
monitoring.tpl.pod_network_rx_bytes.desc: Pod inbound traffic rate. Sources: S3 pulls, AllReduce from other ranks, kubelet heartbeats. With 4-rank DDP training, traffic should be balanced across ranks; a sudden spike on one rank = it is pulling extra data (possibly slow).
monitoring.tpl.pod_network_tx_bytes.desc: Pod outbound traffic rate. AllReduce sends + checkpoint uploads + monitoring reports.
monitoring.tpl.pod_oom_events.descriptio: Cumulative rate of Pod containers being OOMKilled. Anything > 0 = you must adjust the limits or reduce the batch size.
monitoring.tpl.pod_oom_events.title: OOM Events
monitoring.tpl.pod_phase_failed.descript: Whether the Pod is Failed. > 0 = the training failed and terminated.
monitoring.tpl.pod_phase_failed.title: Failed Phase
monitoring.tpl.pod_phase_pending.descrip: Whether the Pod is Pending. 1 for a long time = insufficient resources / scheduling is stuck.
monitoring.tpl.pod_phase_pending.title: Pending Phase
monitoring.tpl.pod_phase_running.descrip: Whether the Pod is in the Running phase (1 = yes, 0 = no). Should be 1 during training.
monitoring.tpl.pod_phase_running.title: Running Phase
monitoring.tpl.pod_processes.description: Total number of processes in the Pod. Python main process + dataloader worker processes = main + num_workers.
monitoring.tpl.pod_processes.title: Process Count
monitoring.tpl.pod_ready.description: Pod Ready condition (all containers Ready). Briefly 0 = it has restarted.
monitoring.tpl.pod_ready.title: Ready
monitoring.tpl.pod_resource_limit_cpu.de: Pod CPU limits (hard runtime cap). Throttling is measured against this.
monitoring.tpl.pod_resource_limit_mem.de: Pod memory limits. The OOMKiller trigger threshold.
Pod CPU requests (the lower bound used for scheduling).
Pod GPU requests (= what K8s actually schedules on).
monitoring.tpl.pod_restart_count.descrip: Cumulative restart count of containers in the Pod. > 0 = it failed and was restarted by K8s; a steadily growing count = repeated crashes, investigate the application/resources immediately.
monitoring.tpl.pod_restart_count.title: Restart Count
monitoring.tpl.pod_scheduled.description: Whether the Pod was scheduled successfully. Long Pending + scheduled = 0 = scheduling failed (no resources / node affinity not satisfied).
monitoring.tpl.pod_scheduled.title: Scheduled
monitoring.tpl.pod_sockets.description: Number of sockets open in the Pod (NCCL / RDMA / S3 client).
monitoring.tpl.pod_sockets.title: Socket Count
monitoring.tpl.pod_spec_cpu_quota.descri: cgroup CPU quota (converted to cores). Corresponds to limits.cpu; compare it against throttled.
monitoring.tpl.pod_spec_cpu_quota.title: CPU Quota
monitoring.tpl.pod_spec_mem_limit.title: Memory Limit
monitoring.tpl.pod_threads.description: Total number of threads in the Pod. PyTorch DataLoader workers + intra-op threads = num_workers × N.
monitoring.tpl.pod_threads.title: Thread Count
monitoring.tpl.pod_threads_max.title: Thread Limit
monitoring.tpl.pod_unschedulable.descrip: Whether the Pod is marked unschedulable (1 = yes). Set when Kueue refuses admission or resources are insufficient.
monitoring.tpl.pod_unschedulable.title: Unschedulable
monitoring.tpl.ray_component_cpu.descrip: CPU usage of each Ray component process (Component of ray_component_cpu_percentage: raylet/agent/gcs_server/ray::* etc.).
monitoring.tpl.ray_component_cpu.title: Component CPU% (by Component)
monitoring.tpl.ray_component_mem.descrip: RSS memory of each Ray component process (ray_component_rss_mb).
monitoring.tpl.ray_component_mem.title: Component Memory RSS (by Component)
monitoring.tpl.ray_cpu_used.description: Logical CPU resources used from Ray's scheduling view (ray_resources Name=CPU State=USED).
monitoring.tpl.ray_cpu_used.title: Ray Logical CPU Used
monitoring.tpl.ray_dashboard_qps.descrip: Ray dashboard API request rate (rate of ray_dashboard_api_requests_count_requests_total).
monitoring.tpl.ray_dashboard_qps.title: Dashboard API QPS
monitoring.tpl.ray_gpu_used.description: Logical GPU resources used from Ray's scheduling view (ray_resources Name=GPU State=USED). 0 for CPU tasks.
monitoring.tpl.ray_gpu_used.title: Ray Logical GPU Used
monitoring.tpl.ray_object_store_avail.de: Available memory of the Ray plasma object store (ray_object_store_available_memory).
monitoring.tpl.ray_object_store_used.des: Used memory of the Ray plasma object store (ray_object_store_used_memory).
monitoring.tpl.ray_spilled_bytes.descrip: Bytes of objects spilled to disk (ray_spill_manager_objects_bytes). Steadily growing = the object store does not have enough memory.
monitoring.tpl.ray_spilled_bytes.title: Spilled to Disk
monitoring.tpl.ray_worker_failures.descr: Cumulative number of unplanned worker process crashes (ray_unintentional_worker_failures_total). Rising during long-running training = OOM/node faults; catch them early.
monitoring.tpl.ray_worker_failures.title: Worker Unexpected Crashes (Total)
monitoring.tpl.ray_worker_startup_fail.d: Cumulative number of times the scheduler failed to start a worker (ray_scheduler_failed_worker_startup_total). Steadily increasing = image/resource/runtime environment problems.
monitoring.tpl.training_auto_restart.des: Number of automatic recoveries by the operator. 1-2 is normal (node jitter); frequent (>5) = the node has a hardware problem and should be taken offline.
monitoring.tpl.training_auto_restart_dow: Cumulative time spent on automatic recovery. Low = recovery is fast.
monitoring.tpl.training_fault_count.desc: Total number of faults detected during training. 0 = healthy. 1-2 occasional faults (sporadic NCCL jitter) are acceptable; a steadily growing count = the cluster is unstable.
Cumulative manual interruption time in ms.
monitoring.tpl.training_manual_restart.d: Number of manual restarts by an admin. Should be 0 (auto-resume takes over). Non-zero = auto recovery failed and someone intervened.
monitoring.tpl.training_operator_jobs_cr: Cumulative number of jobs the Training Operator created for this task (including re-creations).
monitoring.tpl.training_operator_jobs_de: Cumulative number of jobs the Training Operator deleted.
monitoring.tpl.training_operator_jobs_ma: Cumulative number of jobs the Training Operator handed to Kueue for scheduling.
monitoring.tpl.training_operator_jobs_su: Cumulative number of jobs the Training Operator marked as succeeded.
monitoring.tpl.training_time_ms.descript: Actual total training time in milliseconds (excluding fault/recovery periods). Compare with wall clock time to get uptime%.
monitoring.tpl.training_time_ms.title: Total Training Time
monitoring.tpl.training_uptime_percentag: Percentage of total time the training was actually running. 100 = never interrupted; 95 = 3 minutes of every hour spent recovering. Below 80% means the hardware is unstable and auto-resume is happening frequently.
